question: which centre saw the biggest fall in attendance rate from 2023 to 2024
gold_sql: WITH combined AS (SELECT "Centre" AS centre, 2023 AS year, "Avg Daily Present" / "Enrolled Kids" * 100.0 AS rate FROM attendance_2023 UNION ALL SELECT centre_name AS centre, 2024 AS year, average_attendance / enrolment * 100.0 AS rate FROM attendance_2024) , by_year AS (SELECT centre, AVG(CASE WHEN year = 2023 THEN rate END) AS avg_2023, AVG(CASE WHEN year = 2024 THEN rate END) AS avg_2024 FROM combined GROUP BY centre) SELECT centre, avg_2023 - avg_2024 AS drop_pp FROM by_year ORDER BY drop_pp DESC, centre LIMIT 1
sql_duckdb: WITH attendance_data AS (SELECT "Centre" AS centre, "Month" AS month, "Enrolled Kids" AS enrolment, "Avg Daily Present" AS attendance, 2023 AS year FROM "attendance_2023" UNION ALL SELECT "centre_name" AS centre, "month" AS month, "enrolment" AS enrolment, "average_attendance" AS attendance, 2024 AS year FROM "attendance_2024"), yearly_rates AS (SELECT centre, year, CAST("Avg Daily Present" AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(NULLIF("Enrolled Kids", 0), 0) AS attendance_rate FROM (SELECT centre, year, SUM(attendance) AS "Avg Daily Present", SUM(enrolment) AS "Enrolled Kids" FROM attendance_data GROUP BY centre, year)), rate_changes AS (SELECT r2023.centre, (r2024.attendance_rate - r2023.attendance_rate) AS rate_change FROM yearly_rates AS r2023 JOIN yearly_rates AS r2024 ON r2023.centre = r2024.centre WHERE r2023.year = 2023 AND r2024.year = 2024) SELECT centre FROM rate_changes ORDER BY rate_change ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

You translate ordinary questions into exactly one read-only DuckDB SELECT or WITH query.

Return SQL only. Never write files, install software, calculate values yourself, or invent columns.

Use only the supplied schema. Preserve relevant scope from earlier turns unless the newest question changes it.

A requested rate must use its stated numerator and denominator. Percentage-point change means later percentage minus earlier percentage, not relative growth.

When the user explicitly asks for percent or percentage, multiply numerator divided by denominator by 100.

When the user asks to compare years or groups without asking for a change, keep those year/group columns and requested measures in the output.

When several known category values are named, filter them separately with IN rather than concatenating them.

Use NULLIF for denominators. Missing values remain missing and are not zero.

Quote column names with double quotes when they contain spaces or odd characters. When two tables describe the same thing with different column names, UNION ALL them with aligned aliases.

For approximate name matching across tables use jaro_winkler_similarity(lower(trim(a)), lower(trim(b))) >= 0.9.

CURRENT QUESTION:
which centre saw the biggest fall in attendance rate from 2023 to 2024
attempts.response:
```sql
WITH attendance_data AS (
  SELECT
    "Centre" AS centre,
    "Month" AS month,
    "Enrolled Kids" AS enrolment,
    "Avg Daily Present" AS attendance,
    2023 AS year
  FROM "attendance_2023"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    "centre_name" AS centre,
    "month" AS month,
    "enrolment" AS enrolment,
    "average_attendance" AS attendance,
    2024 AS year
  FROM "attendance_2024"
),
yearly_rates AS (
  SELECT
    centre,
    year,
    CAST("Avg Daily Present" AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF("Enrolled Kids", 0) AS attendance_rate
  FROM (
    SELECT
      centre,
      year,
      SUM(attendance) AS "Avg Daily Present",
      SUM(enrolment) AS "Enrolled Kids"
    FROM attendance_data
    GROUP BY centre, year
  )
),
rate_changes AS (
  SELECT
    r2023.centre,
    (r2024.attendance_rate - r2023.attendance_rate) AS rate_change
  FROM yearly_rates r2023
  JOIN yearly_rates r2024 ON r2023.centre = r2024.centre
  WHERE r2023.year = 2023 AND r2024.year = 2024
)
SELECT
  centre
FROM rate_changes
ORDER BY rate_change ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
